item.title: Germany’s Investor Outlook Reaches Five-Month High After Reforms
item.description: German investor optimism rose to the highest level in five months, a sign of hope that Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s economic reforms will spur growth.

item.title: TSMC to Hike Chip Prices By Up to 10% in 2027, Nikkei Says
item.description: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. has held discussions with clients about chipmaking price increases of as much as 10% in 2027 to cover the rising cost of manufacturing, the Nikkei reported, citing people with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: HSBC’s Kettner Sees Risk of Pullback in Stocks Before Midterms
item.description: Equity investors should look to reduce some exposure after this earnings season, according to HSBC Holdings Plc’s Max Kettner, who warns that stretched sentiment, a fading fiscal impulse, and US midterm election uncertainty could trigger a pullback.

item.title: BlackRock, Hillhouse, Temasek Said Set to Back Innolight Listing
item.description: BlackRock Inc., Hillhouse Investment and Temasek Holdings Pte are set to be among cornerstone investors in the potential $8 billion listing by Zhongji Innolight Co. in Hong Kong, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Euro-Zone Banks Further Tighten Companies’ Credit Standards
item.description: Euro-zone banks tightened corporate credit standards further as they see higher risks due to geopolitical events including the Iran war.

item.title: Gilts Climb as Investors Await More Policy Details From Burnham
item.description: UK government bonds posted small moves as investors awaited fresh policy details from new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, while weak economic data dimmed bets on higher interest rates.

item.title: Spain Is Set to Back BIS’s De Cos for ECB Helm, Expansion Says
item.description: The Spanish government plans to back Pablo Hernández de Cos as its candidate for the presidency of the European Central Bank, Expansión reported.

item.title: London Stock Exchange to Introduce Nonstop Trading Next Year
item.description: The London Stock Exchange will open a new venue outside of its regular market hours, a move to offer “near-continuous trading” and better compete with the 24/7 trading espoused by crypto platforms.

item.title: Indonesia Markets First Panda Bonds as It Broadens Funding
item.description: Indonesia has begun marketing its inaugural yuan-denominated bonds in China’s domestic debt market, as Southeast Asia’s largest economy seeks to diversify funding sources amid currency volatility and fiscal challenges.

item.title: Iran War Forces Cash-Strapped Asian Nations to Buy Expensive LNG
item.description: Pakistan and Bangladesh were forced to buy some of their most expensive liquefied natural gas shipments in years as the Middle East conflict chokes supply, straining government finances and prompting both countries to rethink their reliance on the super-chilled fuel.

item.title: Another Tanker Hit in Hormuz as Houthis Add to Regional Risks
item.description: Another tanker was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz as renewed hostilities empty the waterway, while a threat by Houthi rebels to blockade Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea heightened regional maritime risks.

item.title: UK Borrowing Overshoots in Warning to New Burnham Government
item.description: Britain borrowed more than forecast in the first three months of the fiscal year, a reminder to new Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey of the challenges he faces to keep the public finances on track.

item.title: UK Labor Market Holds Steady Ahead of BOE Decision
item.description: Britain’s labor market showed further signs of stabilizing in June, according to data published the week before the Bank of England’s next interest rate decision.

item.title: FTSE 100 Live: Pound Steady After Healey Named Chancellor
item.description: FTSE 100 Live: Pound Steady After Healey Named Chancellor【原文：FTSE 100 Live: Pound Steady After Healey Named Chancellor】

item.title: Merz Gets a Chance to Reset His Chancellorship After Ally Quits
item.description: The 48-hour firestorm that took down one of German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s key parliamentary allies has given him a window to tighten his grip on the policymaking apparatus.

item.title: Moody’s Sees State’s Arrears Keeping Kenya’s Bad Loans Elevated
item.description: Kenya’s biggest lenders are saddled with a stubborn asset-quality bottleneck: a mountain of state arrears that is chocking private-sector liquidity and keeping bad loans high, even as overall banking conditions improve.

item.title: Palm Slips from Month-High as Weak Crude Dents Biofuel Appeal
item.description: Palm oil fell from a near one-month high following weakness in the crude and vegetable oil complex, denting the appeal of biofuels.

item.title: Hungary Set for Another Rate Cut as Inflation Stays Muted
item.description: Hungary’s central bank is poised to lower borrowing costs for a second straight month as subdued inflation allows policymakers to press ahead with their monetary easing cycle.

item.title: Iran War Risk Set to Keep African Interest Rates Higher for Longer
item.description: African policymakers are set to keep interest rates higher for longer as renewed hostilities between the US and Iran fan fresh inflation fears, especially in countries that are net fuel importers.

item.title: Turkish Airlines Exploring Acquisitions in Asia, South America
item.description: Turkish Airlines is exploring more acquisition opportunities as it looks to expand its global reach.

item.title: Won Daily Trading Volume Jumps on Extended Hours, Stock Selloff
item.description: Daily trading volume in the South Korean won has picked up since 24-hour trading began two weeks ago, a trend driven by foreigners offloading local chipmakers’ shares.

item.title: Japan Insurers Buy Most Super-Long Bonds in Three Years in June
item.description: Japanese insurance firms bought the most super-long government bonds in three years last month, adding to signs that demand from a key buyer is stabilizing.

item.title: Iron Ore Drops as China Steel Losses Deepen, Hormuz Risks Rise
item.description: Iron ore fell for a second day as deteriorating profit margins at Chinese steel mills and continued US-Iran hostilities clouded the demand outlook.

item.title: Japan Releases Fiscal Plan Without Answer on Sales Tax Issue
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s administration finally approved an annual economic and fiscal policy plan that cites the independence of the central bank while leaving unresolved the issue of a costly sales tax cut on food.

item.title: Goldman Says Brent Could Top $120 If Hormuz Disruptions Persist
item.description: Brent could rally to more than $120 a barrel by the fourth quarter if disruptions of the Strait of Hormuz persist, according to Goldman Sachs Group Inc., although that’s not the bank’s base case.

item.title: Samsung Hires Ex-Boston Dynamics Executive in Robotics Push
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co. has hired one of South Korea’s leading robotics executives from Hyundai Motor Group to oversee a new robotics division, escalating competition in a sector emerging as the next battleground among global technology companies.

item.title: North Korea’s Trade With China Soars to Highest Level Since 2017
item.description: North Korea’s trade with China jumped to its highest level since sweeping sanctions were imposed in 2017, as the neighbors move to restore ties after years of Pyongyang’s deepening partnership with Moscow.

item.title: Global Investors Turn Cautious on Indian Bonds
item.description: The rupee is also under strain, with slowing debt inflows coinciding with renewed foreign selling in stocks.

item.title: China Broadens Market Rescue With Tech Stocks Drawing Support
item.description: China is stepping up efforts to stabilize its stock market, mobilizing a range of state-linked institutions to stem a tech-driven selloff. The chip-heavy STAR 50 index extended gains.

item.title: China Vows to Achieve Annual Growth Target After Economy Weakens
item.description: China’s cabinet pledged to ensure the country will meet its full-year economic goal and to forge ahead with implementing policies, after growth slipped below the official target range in the second quarter.
